sentences.text: Ordinary Civil Suit.

1.1 Facts as averred in the plaint are that the Plaintiff is the Sole Proprietor of Shudh Garhwal Paneer Nirmata Sangh, which is engaged in the business of distribution, manufacturing and supplying of milk and other milk products such as ghee, dana khoya, cooking cream, paneer, butter,
cheese etc.
It is stated that Plaintiff has been engaged in this business for past 27 years and is a distributor and supplier to numerous Five Star Hotels and Government Bodies of India.

sentences.text: It is stated that the present suit is being filed through Mr. Manik Saha, Junior Manager, who was authorized vide Authorization letter dated 17.04.2017.
It is further stated that Defendant is engaged in the business of catering services.

It is stated that in March, 2011, the Defendant approached and made representation for purchase, supply and delivery of milk and various milk products to be supplied and delivered to the addresses i.e. (i) Chelmsford Club,
1-Raisina Road, New Delhi, (ii) 2 nd Floor, 214-216, S.F. DDA Commercial Complex, Aurobindo Place Market, Hauz Khas, New Delhi; and (iii) C-600, Defence Colony, Delhi, where the Defendant company was providing catering services.

It is stated that as per the representation made by the Defendant, the Plaintiff agreed to supply milk and various milk products on various dates as per day to day demands and requirements of the Defendant company at the aforesaid venues.

It is stated that the Defendant company agreed that upon supply and delivery of products by the Plaintiff, any concerned person or employee of Defendant would sign/stamp and acknowledge the delivery of products to which the Plaintiff would raise consolidated monthly invoices at the end of the month.
It was further agreed that the invoices raised by the Plaintiff would be cleared within 15 days from its receipt and failure to pay or clear the invoice would attract and accrue interest @18% p.a.
It is stated that as per the requirements of the Defendant, the Plaintiff started supply of milk and milk products to Defendant from April, 2011 onwards at the venues.
It is stated that the present suit is filed with respect to the outstanding dues for the products supplied at venue Chem's Ford Club, 1 Raisina Road, New Delhi.

It is stated that the challans are acknowledged by the staff/ employee of the Defendant company namely Sh. Rahul, Sh. Rajendra, Sh. Vinod Kumar and Sh. Saurabh, who were present at the said venue at the time of delivery of products by the Plaintiff.

It is further stated that milk and milk products supplied and delivered by the Plaintiff were as per the various requirements and demands placed upon the Plaintiff from time to time and produces were received by the Defendant as per their satisfaction and never returned to the Plaintiff as defective product.

It is stated that from April, 2011 till February, 2013, the Defendant company had placed numerous orders on the Plaintiff which the Plaintiff delivered without delay and compromise on the quality of its products.

It is stated that on the basis of signed/ stamped and acknowledged challans by the employees of the Defendant company, the Plaintiff raised consolidated invoices which were duly acknowledged by the Defendant company.
It is stated that the Defendant initially made payments on the invoice value but later on the Defendant started making on account payments.
It is stated that from April 2011 to February 2013, the Plaintiff had supplied products worth Rs.38,27,318/- at the Chemsford Club, for which challans and invoices were raised from time to time.

It is stated that the Plaintiff made last supply to the Defendant on 06.02.2013 vide Challan no. 02/13/AA2866 at the aforementioned venue and the Plaintiff raised last consolidated invoice on the Defendant on 06.02.2013 bearing Serial no. TI- 16260 for a sum of Rs.1,215.90/-, which was still outstanding and due and payable.

It is stated that thereafter, the Plaintiff was constrained to stop supplying the milk Sh. Ashwani Kumar vs M/S Bee Gee Catering Private Limited on 3 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149742891/
2 and milk products at all the venues of the Defendant.

sentences.text: It is stated that the Defendant made part payments of the invoices from 01.03.2013 till 19.12.2015 and the Defendant company made an account part payment of Rs.10,000/- on 19.12.2014 towards invoices.
It is stated that on 28.04.2015, the Defendant issued a cheque no. 135772, drawn on Corporation Bank for a sum of Rs.50,000/- which returned back dishonoured.
It is further submitted that an admitted sum of Rs.6,13,190/- alongwith interest @18% p.a. was still outstanding, due and payable by the Defendant to the Plaintiff.

It is stated that the Plaintiff repeatedly contacted the Director of the Defendant company and requested him to clear the outstanding amount but the Defendant sought extension of time and evaded its liability.

It is stated that the Plaintiff issued a legal notice on 11.09.2016 upon Defendant company calling upon it to pay an amount of Rs.9,13,460/- alongwith interest @18% p.a.
till its realization.
It is stated that the said legal notice was for consolidated amount dues qua all the venues where the Plaintiff supplied the products to Defendant company.
On these grounds, the present suit is filed seeking recovery of Rs.6,13,190/- alongwith interest from the Defendant.
2. Summons of the suit were issued to the Defendant.
Upon service of summons, the Defendant appeared and filed its written statement.

It is stated in the written statement that the present suit is without any cause of action; that the plaint has not been verified as per law; that the suit has not been filed by the duly authorized person.

It is stated that the Plaintiff was seeking recovery of Rs.6,13,190/- on the premise of having allegedly supplied various materials, however, none of the bills produced by the Plaintiff had any acknowledgment of materials being supplied.
It is stated that unilateral raising of invoices including the last invoice of 06.03.2013 was only a ploy to bring the present suit within the period of limitation.
It is further stated that none of the invoices were accompanied with the orders to support said invoices.

It is stated that the alleged payment of Rs.10,000/- on 19.12.2014 and issuance of cheque dated 28.04.2015 were manipulated documents as blank signed cheques were given by the Defendant to the Plaintiff at the time of entering into business proposals in 2011-2012.
2.1. On merits, it is stated that the acknowledgment on the challans were doctored and manipulated by the Plaintiff.

It is stated that Defendant had made payments of all the invoices through which the material was supplied to Defendant and after the settlement of all invoices, the Plaintiff had made a false claim upon the Defendant.
All other pleadings made in the plaint were denied by the Defendant.
On these grounds, it is prayed that the present suit be dismissed.

sentences.text: I have heard the arguments advanced by Ld. Counsel for the Plaintiff and gone through the material available on record.

My issue-wise findings are as under:-
8. Issue no. 3 Whether the suit is without any cause of action?

OPD. 
Onus to prove this issue was upon the Defendant.

Perusal of the record reflects that apart from merely averring in the written statement no steps have been taken by the Defendant to rebut the evidence led by the Plaintiff in the present case nor has the Defendant led any defence evidence despite several opportunities to prove its contentions.
It is not a case that the Defendant is not aware of the present suit but has chosen not to pursue the matter to its finality.

In the absence of any corroborative proof or evidence led by the Defendant, this issue is decided against the Defendant as the Plaintiff has prima facie placed on record invoices seeking recovery of an amount of Rs.6,13,190/- from the Defendant.
9. Issue no. 4
Whether the suit of the plaintiff is barred by limitation?

OPD. 
Onus to prove this issue was upon the Defendant.

The Defendant has averred in the written statement that the present suit is barred by limitation on the ground that none of the bills produced has any acknowledgment of the Defendant and have been unilaterally raised with the last invoice dated 06.02.2013 being Ex. PW2/1 being placed on record in order to extend the period of limitation.
The Plaintiff has also placed cheque of Rs.50,000/- dated 28.04.2015.
Perusal of the record, however, shows that the Plaintiff has placed original invoices on record alongwith a cheque of part payment.
The present suit was filed in 2017.

No evidence has been led by the Defendant to support its contentions nor have the Plaintiff's witnesses been cross-examined by the Defendant despite opportunities to discharge its onus that the suit has barred by limitation as contended.
Therefore, in the considered opinion of the Court, the present case has been filed by the Plaintiff within the prescribed period of limitation i.e. 25.04.2017.
This issue is accordingly decided against the Defendant.
10. Issue no. 5 and 6 Whether the suit has not been filed by duly authorized person?
OPD Whether the plaint has not been verified in accordance with law?
OPD 10.1 Both these issues are decided together being inter- connected.
Onus to prove these issues was upon the Defendant.

It is the case of the Defendant that the present suit has not been filed by the duly authorized person and the alleged authorization is not proper and has not been properly verified in accordance with law.

Perusal of the record reflects that present suit has been filed by Mr. Ashwani Kumar, who is the Sole proprietor of Shudh Garhwal Paneer Nirmata Sangh and has authorized Mr. Manik Saha to institute the present suit.

The present suit has been signed and verified by Mr. Manik Saha as the authorized signatory/
representative.
The Authorization Letter in favour of Mr. Manik Saha is Ex. PW1/1.

No questions have been put pertaining to this document by the Defendant as despite opportunities during the examination of both the Plaintiff Witnesses and the Defendant have accordingly failed to show that the suit was not filed by a duly authorized person or was verified in accordance with law.
The Defendant did not appear for the cross-examination of any of the Plaintiff's witnesses.

11. Issue no. 1 and 2 Issue No. 1 - Whether the plaintiff is entitled to a decree for sum of Rs.6,13,190/- from the defendant as prayed for? OPP Issue No. 2 - Whether plaintiff is entitled to any interest?
If so at what rate and for what period? OPP 11.1.
Both these issues are decided together being inter- connected.

Perusal of the plaint reflects that the Plaintiff has filed the present suit seeking recovery of Rs.6,13,190/- against the Defendant on the ground that the Plaintiff and the Defendant had various transactions where the Plaintiff supplied milk and milk products to Defendant at his venue at Chemsford Club and despite challans and consolidated invoices, the Defendant failed to make payment.

In its written statement, the Defendant has urged that Plaintiff has been unilaterally raising invoices and all the invoices were acknowledged and Defendant had made payment of all the invoices and after settlement of invoices, the Plaintiff has filed a false suit.
The Plaintiff has examined two witnesses in support of his contentions.
PW1 Manik Saha, being the Authorized signatory and PW2 Arun Gupta, who is working as the Accounts Manager.

It is pertinent to mention that both the witnesses were not cross-examined by the Defendant despite opportunities being given and Defendant did not lead any evidence despite being granted opportunities and adjournments.
Perusal of the record reflects that the Plaintiff has placed on record various invoices from Ex. PW1/1 to Ex. PW1/82, which prima facie contain signatures on behalf of the Defendant.
Perusal of the these invoices further reflects that they contain the description of books, quantity and price and the address of the Defendant company.
The careful and meaningful reading of the aforesaid delivery challan Ex.PW-1/3 to Ex.PW-1/85 further reflect the signature on behalf of the Defendant along with date.

It is significant to mention that these invoices are duly supported by certificate under Section 65 B of Indian Evidence Act Ex.PW-1/90. PW-2 namely Arun Gupta has also placed on record invoices Ex.PW-2/2 toEx.PW-2/12 along with certificate under Section 65 B of Indian Evidence Act, Ex.PW-2/23 to corroborate their contentions that the Plaintiff and Defendant were continuously doing business dealing with each other.

11.2 Despite opportunities being given, Defendant did not opt to lead any evidence or to cross-examined the Plaintiff witnesses so as to prove their contentions as raised in the Written Statement that the Defendant has paid the entire amount and was no liable to pay any outstanding amount as claimed by the Plaintiff in the present suit.
Furthermore, perusal of the documents reflects that invoices were generated regularly pursuant to the business transactions between the parties and the delivery challans annexed with the plaint.

In fact, it has been duly proved during trial and the evidence placed on record by the Plaintiff that that material was duly supplied regularly by the Plaintiff to the Defendant against acknowledgement during the course of business transaction.

The Plaintiff has also sent legal notice dated 11.09.2016 Ex.PW-1/87 raising the demand of Rs.
9,13,460/- and the Plaintiff has also placed on record ledger account maintained qua the Defendant Ex.PW-2/14.
In fact, it is significant to mention that the PW-1/86 is the cheque issued on behalf of the Defendant to the Plaintiff dated 28.04.2015 for Rs. 50,000/- which as per the plaint was dishonored.

As already reiterated above, despite opportunities the Defendant did not appear to contest the present case and did not cross-examine the plaintiff witness or to lead any defence evidence during trial.

Plaintiff has been able to prima facie show that there was regular business Sh. Ashwani Kumar vs M/S Bee Gee Catering Private Limited on 3 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149742891/
6 transactions between the parties and the plaintiff has raised various invoices for which payment is still to be paid by the Defendant.

In view of the aforesaid facts and discussions

12. The Hon'ble Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Pt. Munshi Ram &
Associates (P) Ltd. v. DDA, 2010 SCC Online Del 2444 has held that higher rates of interest, which are against public policy, can be struck down by the Court by finding such rates of interest to be against the pub- lic policy.

The Hon'ble Single Bench has granted 9%
per annum interest instead of 24 % per annum i.e. 2% per month.

13. In the considered opinion of this court, the interest of 24% per annum as claimed is unreasonable and excessive in terms of the Judgments of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi and is also against public policy and void under Section 23 of the In- dian Contract Act, 1872.
In the present case, the interest of jus- tice would be served if the Plaintiff is granted a simple interest @ 9 % per annum from the date of legal notice dated 11.09.2016 till the final realization.
RELIEF 14.
From the discussions, as adumbrated hereinabove, I hereby pass the following FINAL ORDER (A).

A decree of Rs.6,13,190/- is passed in favour of the Plain- tiff and against the Defendant along with simple interest @ 9% per annum from the date of legal notice dated 11.09.2016 till fil- ing of the case.

The Plaintiff is also granted pendent-lite simple rate of interest @ 6% per annum and future simple rate of inter- est @ 9 % per annum till its realization and the same are also payable by the Defendant.
(B) The cost of the suit is also awarded in favour of the Plaintiff and against the Defendant.
Decree-sheet be prepared accordingly.
File be consigned to record room.
